messages.text: How do changes in Wi-Fi 7/8 technology affect the measurement capability required from Signal Generator / Signal Analyzer?

Wi‑Fi 7/8 pushes Signal Generator / Signal Analyzer requirements mainly in **bandwidth, modulation quality, multi-channel synchronization, antenna/MIMO capability, and signaling realism**.

### What changes in Wi‑Fi 7/8 drive new measurement needs?

| Technology change | Impact on Signal Generator / Analyzer capability |
|---|---|
| **Wider channels**: Wi‑Fi 7 supports up to **320 MHz** channels; R&S notes Wi‑Fi 8 retains bandwidths up to 320 MHz and has candidate waveforms such as **480 MHz** | Generator and analyzer need **instantaneous RF bandwidth beyond 320 MHz**, ideally ~500 MHz class for future-proofing. R&S cites CMP180 support up to **500 MHz bandwidth** and 480 MHz WLAN waveform verification. |
| **Higher modulation**: **4096QAM** | Requires much lower EVM, higher modulation accuracy, better phase noise, linearity, dynamic range, and analyzer accuracy. |
| **MLO — Multi-Link Operation** | Test system needs **multiple RF chains**, synchronized generation/analysis across bands or channels, and the ability to validate simultaneous links. |
| **Higher throughput / advanced spatial multiplexing** | Analyzer/generator platform must handle high data rates, multiple streams, and many antenna ports. R&S describes CMX500 as supporting up to **20 Gbps**, wide dynamic range, 4096QAM, and up to **16 device antenna ports**. |
| **Wi‑Fi 8 new PHY/MAC features** | Measurement setup must be upgradeable for new RF signaling and physical-layer validation, not only static waveform generation. R&S notes added Wi‑Fi 8 testing capability on CMX500 to validate prototype Wi‑Fi 8 devices and unique PHY features. |
| **R&D vs production split** | R&D needs signaling-mode, real-world behavior, MLO and OTA testing; production needs fast non-signaling RF test with wideband generation/analysis. |

### Practical implication for Signal Generators

For Wi‑Fi 7/8, the signal generator should support:

- **Up to 7.125 GHz frequency coverage** for 6 GHz band testing.
- **At least 320 MHz modulation bandwidth**, preferably **500 MHz-class** for Wi‑Fi 8 candidate waveforms.
- **4096QAM waveform quality**, with low EVM contribution.
- **Multi-channel / multi-link generation** for MLO.
- **Phase-coherent or synchronized RF outputs** where MLO, MIMO, or OTA testing requires it.
- Support for both **non-signaling waveform generation** and, where needed, integration with signaling testers.

### Practical implication for Signal Analyzers

The analyzer side needs:

- **Wide instantaneous analysis bandwidth**: 320 MHz minimum; 480/500 MHz capability is valuable for Wi‑Fi 8 readiness.
- **High dynamic range and low residual EVM** to measure 4096QAM accurately.
- **Multi-channel capture / correlation** for MLO and multi-radio behavior.
- **Advanced demodulation support** for Wi‑Fi 7 and emerging Wi‑Fi 8 PHY features.
- **OTA/MIMO measurement support**, especially for devices with multiple antennas and spatial streams.

### R&S context from the knowledge base

- R&S states Wi‑Fi 8 keeps key Wi‑Fi 7 PHY parameters: operation up to **7.125 GHz**, bandwidths up to **320 MHz**, **4096QAM**, and **MLO**, while adding new PHY/MAC technologies that create new testing hurdles.  
  Source: `raw/Productions/PR/Rohde & Schwarz and Broadcom showcase first Wi-Fi 8 RF signaling tests, paving way for next-gen connectivity.md`

- R&S positions the **CMP180** for non-signaling R&D/production testing, supporting Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to **8 GHz** with bandwidths up to **500 MHz**, and demonstrating a **480 MHz WLAN waveform** as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 candidate.  
  Source: `raw/Productions/PR/Rohde & Schwarz presents its Wi-Fi 7 multi-channel single-box test solutions for R&D and production at MWC 2024.md`

- For Wi‑Fi 7 MLO, R&S says a test environment with **multiple RF chains is crucial**, and positions the **CMX500** as a multi-technology, multi-channel signaling tester for Wi‑Fi 7-specific tests.  
  Source: `raw/Productions/PR/Bluetest and Rohde & Schwarz collaborate to offer over-the-air testing of next-generation WLAN devices.md`

- For Wi‑Fi 8, R&S notes newly added **CMX500 Wi‑Fi 8 testing capabilities** to validate prototype Wi‑Fi 8 devices and demonstrate unique Wi‑Fi 8 physical-layer features.  
  Source: `raw/Productions/PR/Rohde & Schwarz and Broadcom showcase first Wi-Fi 8 RF signaling tests, paving way for next-gen connectivity.md`

### Bottom line

Wi‑Fi 7/8 moves SG/SA requirements from “single wide WLAN channel test” toward **wideband, high-EVM-accuracy, multi-link, multi-RF-chain, multi-antenna, signaling-aware measurement**. A future-proof setup should target **500 MHz-class bandwidth, 4096QAM-grade modulation accuracy, synchronized multi-channel capability, and support for MLO/OTA/MIMO workflows**.

passages.text: In the production phase of WLAN devices, all RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time. Rohde & Schwarz has optimized the [R&S CMP180](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-rf-analyzer-generator/cmp180-radio-communication-tester_63493-1081280.html "CMP180") radio communication tester for this purpose. The instrument supports many cellular and non-cellular technologies including Wi-Fi 6E, Wi-Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz in frequency with bandwidths up to 500 MHz. Leveraging the wide bandwidth, the R&S CMP180 will demonstrate at MWC its ability to verify a WLAN waveform with 480 MHz bandwidth in loopback mode, a potential waveform candidate for the yet-to-be-defined Wi-Fi 8 (IEEE 802.11bn) standard. This feature shows that the cost-effective instrument is future-proof for users not only in production, but also in R&D.

Wi‑Fi 8 retains Wi‑Fi 7 physical-layer parameters such as operation up to 7.125 GHz, channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz, 4096QAM, and Multi-Link Operation, while adding new PHY/MAC technologies that create new testing hurdles [3].
For analyzer/generator bandwidth, R&S shows the R&S CMP180 as a future-proof RF test platform: it supports Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz with bandwidths up to 500 MHz, and it can verify a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 waveform candidate [5].
R&S also states the CMP180 will verify a 480 MHz bandwidth waveform beyond Wi‑Fi 7 requirements, indicating that Wi‑Fi 7/8 evolution requires measurement bandwidth beyond current Wi‑Fi 7 channels [2].
For signaling and multi-link testing, Wi‑Fi 7 MLO makes multiple RF chains crucial in the test environment, and R&S positions the CMX500 as a multi-technology, multi-channel signaling tester with integrated Wi‑Fi 7 test functionality for Wi‑Fi 7-specific tests [6].
For Wi‑Fi 8, R&S is adding CMX500 Wi‑Fi 8 testing capabilities to validate prototype Wi‑Fi 8 devices and demonstrate unique Wi‑Fi 8 physical-layer features [1].
For high-performance RF measurement, the CMX500 is engineered for data rates up to 20 Gbps and supports wide dynamic range, 4096QAM, and up to 16 device antenna ports for advanced spatial multiplexing, covering WLAN including Wi‑Fi 7 and future Wi‑Fi 8 [8].
Thus, the required generator/analyzer capability must scale to wideband waveforms, high-order modulation, multi-band/multi-channel signaling, and many antenna ports in order to cover Wi‑Fi 7 and Wi‑Fi 8 evolution in R&S workflows [3][5][6][8].

Leveraging the wide bandwidth, the R&S CMP180 will demonstrate at MWC its ability to verify a WLAN waveform with 480 MHz bandwidth in loopback mode, a potential waveform candidate for the yet-to-be-defined Wi-Fi 8 (IEEE 802.11bn) standard. This feature shows that the cost-effective instrument is future-proof for users not only in production, but also in R&D.

cited_passages.text: During the development of WLAN devices, measurements of the antennas as well as RF transmitter and receiver characteristics must be conducted under real-world conditions in signaling mode. With MLO being a key feature in Wi-Fi 7, a test environment that provides multiple RF chains is crucial. The R&S CMX500 one-box tester from Rohde & Schwarz, featuring integrated Wi-Fi 7 test functionality, is a multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester. Its flexibility, support for multiple radio technologies, and embedded IP test capabilities make it a versatile solution for a broad range of Wi-Fi 7-specific tests.
